subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Coyote of the Americas
description: A quick, practical guide to Coyote of the Americas.

hook.text: Native American Coyote steals fire, tricks the gods, and sometimes dies from his own schemes. He always returns.

buildup.text: Coyote is greedy, lustful, foolish, and brilliant—often in the same story. He's the most human of all gods.

discovery.text: In Navajo tradition, Coyote scattered the stars carelessly. That's why constellations aren't perfectly ordered.

twist.text: Coyote's failures teach more than his wins. He shows what happens when cleverness lacks wisdom.

climax.text: Coyote can't be destroyed because chaos can't be eliminated. He's the flaw in every perfect system.

punchline.text: Kill him. He comes back. Always.

quiz.question: Why are constellations imperfect in Navajo tradition?
